title: Spinlock (busy-wait lock)
summary: A spinlock is a lock where the acquiring thread busy-waits (spins) until the lock is available. Implementation: atomic test-and-set (TAS) or compare-and-swap (CAS). On contention, the thread spins (wastes CPU) but avoids context switch overhead. Used for short critical sections (< 100ns). Variants: ticket lock (FIFO fairness), MCS lock (queue-based, cache-friendly), CLH lock (list-based).

structure.meaning: Atomically set lock to 1 and return old value. If old value was 0, lock acquired. If 1, spin.
Atomically compare lock with expected value; if equal, set to new value. Returns success/failure.
FIFO fairness: each thread gets a ticket number. Threads acquire lock in ticket order. Prevents starvation.
Queue-based: each thread spins on its own cache line (not a shared variable). Cache-friendly. Used in Linux kernel.
List-based: each thread spins on its predecessor's node. Simpler than MCS.
Spin for a while, then sleep (yield to OS). Balances latency and CPU usage.

notes: Spinlocks are used for very short critical sections (< 100ns).
MCS locks are cache-friendly (each thread spins on its own cache line).
Ticket locks provide FIFO fairness (prevent starvation).
Linux kernel uses spinlocks (with preemption disabled) for short critical sections.
